examples.ko: 저는 어릴 때부터 코미디언이 되고 싶었어요.
examples.en: I wanted to be a comedian since I was little.
That comedian makes people laugh with just his expression.
I saw a famous comedian on TV yesterday.

examples.ko: 코미디언 친구가 생일 파티에서 노래를 불렀어요.
examples.en: My comedian friend sang a song at the birthday party.
If you talk like a comedian, the mood loosens up quickly.

examples.ko: 우리 반에는 코미디언 같은 학생이 한 명 있어요.
examples.en: There is one student in our class who is like a comedian.

explain: 방송에서는 '개그맨', '개그우먼'이라는 말을 더 자주 써요. 코미디언은 성별과 상관없이 쓸 수 있어서 소개할 때 안전한 말이에요. 재미있는 친구에게는 보통 '웃긴 사람'이라고 해요.
explain_en: On Korean TV people often say 개그맨 and 개그우먼. 코미디언 works for any gender, so it is a safe word when you introduce someone. For a funny friend, people usually just say 웃긴 사람.

examples.en: We caught clams on the tidal flat of the West Sea.
When the water goes out, the mud flat is exposed widely.
The kids took off their shoes and walked on the mud flat.
You need to book the mud flat experience for the weekend.

examples.ko: 갯벌에는 게와 작은 생물이 많이 살아요.
examples.en: Many crabs and small creatures live on tidal flats.
I woke up early to take photos of the tidal flat.

explain: '해변'은 모래가 있는 바닷가이고, 갯벌은 진흙이 넓게 펼쳐진 곳이에요. 밀물과 썰물 때문에 하루에 두 번 모습이 바뀌어서, 가기 전에 물때를 확인해야 해요. 서해안에 특히 넓어요.
explain_en: 해변 is a sandy shore, while 갯벌 is a wide stretch of mud. The tide changes it twice a day, so check the tide times (물때) before you go. The west coast has especially big ones.

examples.ko: 우리 다 같이 건배해요! 새해 복 많이 받으세요.
examples.en: Let's all raise our glasses! Happy New Year.

examples.ko: 건배 소리가 식당 안에 크게 울렸어요.
examples.en: The sound of the toast rang out loudly in the restaurant.
The teacher proposed a toast.
We toasted with juice and ate cake.
We wrapped up the gathering with a toast at the end.
When you toast, you clink the glasses lightly.

explain: 한국에서는 '건배!'라고 외치며 잔을 부딪치는 것이 모임의 시작이나 끝 인사 같아요. 술이 아니라 음료수로 해도 괜찮아요. '위하여!'는 누군가를 위해 건배할 때 같이 외쳐요.
explain_en: In Korea, shouting 건배! and clinking glasses is like a greeting at the start or end of a gathering. You can do it with soft drinks too. People also shout 위하여! when toasting to someone or something.

examples.en: My uncle got his high school diploma through an equivalency exam.

examples.ko: 검정고시는 일 년에 두 번 있어요.
examples.en: The equivalency exam is held twice a year.
She prepared for the equivalency exam while working.

examples.ko: 검정고시에 합격해서 대학에 갈 수 있게 됐어요.
examples.en: I passed the equivalency exam, so I could go to university.

examples.ko: 나이가 많아도 검정고시는 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can take the equivalency exam even if you are older.

examples.ko: 검정고시 학원에는 다양한 나이의 사람들이 다녀요.
examples.en: People of many ages attend the equivalency exam academy.

explain: 학교를 다니지 못했거나 중간에 그만둔 사람이 초등학교·중학교·고등학교 졸업 자격을 얻는 시험이에요. 보통 '검정고시를 보다', '검정고시에 합격하다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: This is the exam people take when they missed or left school and still want an elementary, middle or high school graduation qualification. The usual verbs are 검정고시를 보다 and 검정고시에 합격하다.

en: round off; round to the nearest

examples.en: I round off at the first decimal place.
I rounded the result to a whole number.
If you round 3.5, it becomes 4.
I am going to round the scores.
The teacher rounded the average and told us.

examples.ko: 반올림하지 말고 정확한 숫자를 써 주세요.
examples.en: Please write the exact number without rounding.

explain: 숫자를 5 이상이면 올리고 4 이하이면 버리는 계산이에요. 가격이나 평균을 말할 때 많이 써요. 항상 올리는 '올림', 항상 버리는 '버림'과 구별해서 말해요.
explain_en: This is the calculation where 5 and above goes up and 4 and below goes down. It comes up a lot with prices and averages. Do not mix it up with 올림 (always round up) and 버림 (always round down).

examples.en: The floor is cold, so please put down a cushion and sit.
I gave the guest a cushion.
This cushion is thick and soft.
A cushion is placed on the chair.
At the restaurant, we sit on cushions to eat.
Grandma's cushion has a pretty flower pattern.

explain: 방석은 바닥에 앉을 때 깔고, 의자에 놓는 것은 '쿠션'이라고 부르는 경우가 많아요. 한국 식당이나 집에서 바닥에 앉을 때 손님에게 방석을 내줘요. '방석을 깔다', '방석에 앉다'로 써요.
explain_en: 방석 is what you put down to sit on the floor; a soft pad for a chair is often called a 쿠션. In Korean homes and restaurants with floor seating, hosts hand guests a 방석. Typical verbs are 방석을 깔다 and 방석에 앉다.

examples.ko: 두부를 만들 때 생기는 부산물이 비지예요.
examples.en: The by-product of making tofu is called biji.
This factory reuses its by-products.
Refining oil produces several by-products.
If you use by-products well, they become money.

examples.ko: 그 연구의 부산물로 새로운 기술이 나왔어요.
examples.en: A new technology came out as a by-product of that research.
Fruit peels are a by-product of juice.

explain: 공장이나 요리처럼 주된 것을 만들다가 같이 생기는 것을 말해요. 연구나 프로젝트에서 뜻밖에 얻은 좋은 결과에도 비유해서 써요. 쓰고 남는 쓸모없는 것은 '폐기물'이라고 해서 구별해요.
explain_en: It refers to something that comes out alongside the main product, in a factory or in cooking. People also use it figuratively for an unexpected good result of a project. Useless leftovers are called 폐기물, which is a different word.

en: designer; planner (of a structure or system)

examples.en: The designer of this bridge is a foreigner.
The designer revised the drawing again.

examples.ko: 건물 설계자를 직접 만나 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to meet the building's designer in person.

examples.ko: 그는 이 도시를 만든 설계자로 불려요.
examples.en: He is called the designer who created this city.
The designer's ideas show all over the building.
I had a meeting with the program's designer.

explain: 건물, 다리, 기계, 시스템의 구조를 계획하는 사람이에요. 옷이나 포스터를 꾸미는 사람은 '디자이너'라고 하고, 설계자는 구조와 계획 쪽에 써요. 건축 쪽에서는 '건축가'라고도 해요.
explain_en: A 설계자 plans the structure of buildings, bridges, machines or systems. Someone who styles clothes or posters is a 디자이너. In architecture you will also hear 건축가.

examples.en: Old fortress walls remain in Seoul.
In the evening I walked slowly along the fortress wall.
From the top of the wall you can see the whole city.

examples.ko: 이 성곽은 삼백 년 전에 지어졌어요.
examples.en: This fortress wall was built three hundred years ago.

examples.ko: 성곽 길은 사진 찍기 좋은 곳이에요.
examples.en: The wall path is a good place for taking photos.
Tourists climbed up the fortress wall and looked around.

explain: 도시나 궁을 둘러싼 돌담을 말하고, 주로 역사 이야기나 관광 안내에서 써요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '성'이나 '성벽'이라고도 해요. 서울 한양도성이나 수원 화성 같은 곳이 유명해요.
explain_en: It is the stone wall around a city or palace, mostly heard in history talk and tourist guides. In daily speech people also say 성 or 성벽. Seoul's 한양도성 and Suwon's 화성 are famous examples.

examples.en: That soprano's voice is really clear.
My sister took the soprano part in the choir.
A famous soprano is performing in Seoul.
Sopranos sing the high notes.
Alto is more comfortable for me than soprano.
In the opera, the soprano and the tenor sang together.

explain: 여자 목소리 중 가장 높은 음역을 말해요. 낮은 쪽은 '알토', 남자 높은 목소리는 '테너'라고 해요. 합창에서는 '소프라노 파트'처럼 파트 이름으로도 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is the highest range of the female voice. The lower female part is 알토, and the high male voice is 테너. In choirs people often say it as a part name, like 소프라노 파트.

examples.en: Anyway, we have to finish it today.
I don't know the reason, but thanks anyway.
In any case, it would be good to rest now.

examples.ko: 비가 오든 안 오든 여하튼 갈 거예요.
examples.en: Rain or no rain, I will go anyway.
Anyway, that matter is over now.

examples.ko: 여하튼 일단 그 얘기부터 해 봐요.
examples.en: Anyway, let's start with that story first.

explain: '어쨌든', '아무튼'과 거의 같은 뜻인데, 여하튼은 조금 딱딱하고 글에서 더 자주 보여요. 말할 때는 '어쨌든'이나 '아무튼'이 훨씬 자연스러워요. 앞의 이야기를 정리하고 본론으로 돌아갈 때 써요.
explain_en: It is almost the same as 어쨌든 and 아무튼, but 여하튼 sounds a bit stiffer and shows up more in writing. In speech, 어쨌든 or 아무튼 feels more natural. You use it to wrap up a side topic and return to the point.

examples.en: On weekends I rest well at home and recharge.
During my vacation I recharged my body and mind.
Walking improves my mood and recharges me.

examples.ko: 다음 주를 위해 에너지를 재충전할 거예요.
examples.en: I will recharge my energy for next week.

examples.ko: 잠깐 낮잠을 자고 재충전해서 다시 일했어요.
examples.en: I took a short nap, recharged, and worked again.
If you can't recharge, you get tired quickly.

explain: 배터리 같은 물건에는 '충전하다'가 먼저 떠오르고, 사람이 쉬면서 힘을 되찾을 때는 '재충전하다'가 잘 어울려요. 일이나 공부 사이의 휴식을 말할 때 '재충전의 시간'이라는 표현도 써요.
explain_en: For objects like batteries, 충전하다 comes to mind first, while 재충전하다 fits a person resting and getting their strength back. You will also hear the phrase 재충전의 시간 for a break between work or study.

examples.en: An unidentified sound is heard every night.
An unidentified letter was in the mailbox.
Everyone was wary because the man's identity was unknown.

examples.ko: 정체불명의 전화는 받지 않는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's better not to answer calls from unknown numbers.
An unidentified object appeared in the news.

examples.ko: 정체불명 가게에서 이상한 물건을 팔고 있었어요.
examples.en: A mysterious shop was selling strange things.

explain: 주로 '정체불명의 + 명사' 형태로 써요. 누구인지 무엇인지 모르고 조금 수상한 느낌이 있어요. 그냥 모를 때는 '모르는'이라고 하고, '정체불명'은 뉴스나 이야기에서 더 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It mostly appears as 정체불명의 + noun. It carries a slightly suspicious feel, not just not knowing. For ordinary unknowns people say 모르는, while 정체불명 shows up more in news and stories.

examples.en: Our team advanced to the semifinal.

examples.ko: 준결승은 내일 저녁 일곱 시에 시작해요.
examples.en: The semifinal starts at seven tomorrow evening.
We lost the semifinal by a narrow margin.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 준결승까지 한 골도 내주지 않았어요.
examples.en: That player hadn't conceded a single goal until the semifinal.

examples.ko: 준결승 경기를 보러 친구와 경기장에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to the stadium with a friend to watch the semifinal match.
If we win the semifinal, we meet in the final.

explain: 순서는 '예선, 8강, 4강(준결승), 결승'이에요. 스포츠 뉴스에서는 준결승보다 '4강'이라는 말을 더 자주 써요. 준결승에서 진 팀끼리 '3·4위전'을 해요.
explain_en: The order is 예선, 8강, 4강 (준결승), 결승. In sports news 4강 is often used instead of 준결승. The two teams that lose the semifinals play a 3·4위전.

examples.en: My grandfather's hearing has become much weaker.
They tested my hearing at the health checkup.

examples.ko: 큰 소리를 오래 들으면 청력에 해로워요.
examples.en: Listening to loud sounds for a long time is harmful to your hearing.
Cats have better hearing than people.
My hearing got worse, so I bought a hearing aid.
A hearing test doesn't hurt.

explain: '청력이 좋다/나쁘다/약하다'처럼 능력을 말할 때 써요. 같은 종류의 '시력(눈)'이 있어요. 소리를 잘 듣는지 말할 때는 '귀가 밝다/어둡다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is used for the ability itself: 청력이 좋다, 나쁘다, 약하다. Its partner for the eyes is 시력. Informally, people also say 귀가 밝다 or 귀가 어둡다 about someone's hearing.

examples.en: Small fishing boats came into the harbor.
On the weekend I visited a small harbor on the West Sea.
I ate raw fish at a restaurant near the harbor.

examples.ko: 이 포구는 해 질 무렵이 제일 예뻐요.
examples.en: This harbor is prettiest around sunset.
The fishermen left the harbor at dawn.
The harbor village has many quiet alleys.

explain: '항구'보다 작고 정겨운 바닷가 마을 느낌이 있어요. 큰 배가 오가는 곳은 '항구', 어선이 드나드는 작은 곳은 '포구'라고 해요. 여행 글에서 '포구 마을'이라는 말을 자주 봐요.
explain_en: Compared with 항구, 포구 feels smaller and more homey. A big ship port is a 항구, while a small place for fishing boats is a 포구. In travel writing you often see the phrase 포구 마을.

examples.ko: 피자를 먹을 때 피클이 꼭 필요해요.
examples.en: When eating pizza, pickles are a must.
I make cucumber pickles myself.

examples.ko: 피클은 새콤달콤해서 느끼한 음식과 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: Pickles are sweet and sour, so they go well with greasy food.
Please take the pickles out of the hamburger.

examples.ko: 냉장고에 피클 한 병이 남아 있어요.
examples.en: One jar of pickles is left in the fridge.
Pickled radish always comes out at chicken restaurants.

explain: 서양식 새콤달콤한 절임이에요. 한국에서는 치킨이나 피자와 함께 나오는 하얀 '치킨무'도 피클의 한 종류로 봐요. 김치나 장아찌 같은 한국 절임은 피클이라고 하지 않아요.
explain_en: It is the sweet and sour pickle of Western cooking. In Korea the white radish served with fried chicken, 치킨무, counts as a kind of pickle too. Korean pickled foods like 김치 and 장아찌 are not called 피클.

examples.en: One piano key is broken.
The child pressed the keys carefully.
Fingers move quickly over the keys.
There are fewer black keys than white keys.
I wiped the keys clean before playing.
These keys have a soft sound.

explain: 피아노나 오르간에서 손가락으로 누르는 하나하나의 키를 말해요. 컴퓨터 자판은 '키보드'나 '자판'이라고 하고, 건반은 악기에만 써요. '건반 악기'라고 하면 피아노 같은 악기를 한꺼번에 말해요.
explain_en: This is each key you press on a piano or organ. A computer keyboard is a 키보드 or 자판; 건반 is only for instruments. 건반 악기 covers piano-type instruments as a group.

examples.en: I submitted the draft plan to the team leader.
The new plan is much more specific than the last one.
I will explain the draft plan at the meeting.
The budget is missing from the draft plan.
The draft plan I wrote was approved.

examples.ko: 계획안을 한 번 더 고쳐 주세요.
examples.en: Please revise the draft plan one more time.

explain: '계획'은 마음속 생각이나 일정 전체를 말하고, 계획안은 종이나 파일에 적은 '문서'예요. 회사나 학교에서 제출하고 검토하는 글에 써요. '계획서'와 거의 같지만 계획안은 아직 확정 전이라는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: 계획 can be a thought or a whole schedule, while 계획안 is a written document. It is used in companies and schools for something you submit and review. It is close to 계획서, but 계획안 feels not yet final.

en: Korean literature (as a field of study)

examples.en: I majored in Korean literature at university.
In Korean literature class we read old poems.
My younger sibling wants to enter the Korean literature department.
The Korean literature professor recommended a book.

examples.ko: 국문학을 공부하면 한국어를 깊이 이해할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you study Korean literature, you can understand Korean deeply.
He works as a researcher of Korean literature.

explain: 한국 문학을 연구하는 학문이에요. 한국어 자체를 연구하는 '국어학'과 함께 대학에서는 '국어국문학과'로 묶여 있는 경우가 많아요. 외국인에게 한국어를 가르치는 공부는 '한국어교육학'이라서 달라요.
explain_en: It is the field that studies Korean literature. Universities often group it with 국어학 (the study of the Korean language itself) in a 국어국문학과 department. Teaching Korean to foreigners is a different field, 한국어교육학.

examples.en: On autumn nights you can hear crickets.
A cricket came into the room.
The kids searched the grass to catch a cricket.
Crickets make sound by rubbing their wings.
When I hear a cricket's chirp, I feel autumn.
I first saw a cricket at my grandmother's country house.

explain: 귀뚜라미 소리는 한국에서 가을을 알리는 소리로 자주 써요. 소리는 '귀뚤귀뚤'이라고 표현해요. 여름 매미와 짝으로 '매미는 여름, 귀뚜라미는 가을'이라고 느끼는 사람이 많아요.
explain_en: In Korea, cricket sounds often signal autumn. The sound is written as 귀뚤귀뚤. Many people pair it with the summer cicada: 매미 for summer, 귀뚜라미 for fall.

examples.en: My arm stings when I get a shot.
My throat stung, so I took medicine.

examples.ko: 상처에 약을 바르면 조금 따끔할 거예요.
examples.en: It will sting a little when you put medicine on the wound.
My eyes stung and watered.
The teacher gave a stern word.
I was pricked by a needle and my finger stung.

explain: 주사, 소독약, 가시처럼 짧고 찌르는 듯한 아픔에 써요. 오래 계속되는 아픔은 '쑤시다', '욱신거리다'를 써요. '따끔하게 말하다'는 아프도록 엄하게 꾸짖는다는 비유로도 써요.
explain_en: It is for a short, sharp sting from a shot, antiseptic or a thorn. For a lasting ache, use 쑤시다 or 욱신거리다. 따끔하게 말하다 is also used figuratively for scolding someone sharply.

examples.en: My mom braided my hair.
I wear my hair in a long braid.
Braiding your hair is cool and comfortable.
My little sister is braiding the doll's hair.

examples.ko: 끈 세 가닥을 땋아서 팔찌를 만들었어요.
examples.en: I braided three strings to make a bracelet.
I will braid my hair into two plaits.

explain: 머리카락이나 끈을 보통 세 가닥으로 엇갈리게 엮을 때 써요. 'ㅎ' 받침이라 발음이 [따타], '땋아요'로 활용해요. 머리를 묶는 '묶다'와는 달라서 엮는 모양이 생겨야 땋다예요.
explain_en: You use it for weaving hair or cord in an interlaced way, typically with three strands. The ㅎ final makes it sound like [따타], and the polite form is 땋아요. It differs from 묶다 (to tie); 땋다 requires the woven pattern.

examples.en: I saw a famous painting at the art museum.

examples.ko: 이 거실에는 명화 복제품이 걸려 있어요.
examples.en: A reproduction of a famous painting hangs in this living room.

examples.ko: 아버지는 옛날 명화를 보는 걸 좋아하세요.
examples.en: My father likes watching classic films.
The expression of the figure in the masterpiece is interesting.

examples.ko: 주말 저녁에 TV에서 명화를 해 줘요.
examples.en: On weekend evenings the TV shows a classic film.

examples.ko: 그림 한 점이 명화로 알려진 이유가 궁금해요.
examples.en: I wonder why that one picture is known as a masterpiece.

explain: 그림에서는 '널리 알려진 훌륭한 그림', 영화에서는 '오래된 명작 영화'를 말해요. 두 뜻이라 문장 속 말(보다, 걸다, 감상하다)로 구별해요. 예전 TV에서는 '주말의 명화' 같은 프로그램도 있었어요.
explain_en: For paintings it means a widely known great work; for films, an old classic. Because there are two meanings, context verbs like 보다, 걸다 or 감상하다 tell you which. Older TV had programs such as 주말의 명화.

examples.en: It rained a lot and the waterway got blocked.
The farmer made a water channel to the rice field.

examples.ko: 배는 좁은 물길을 따라 천천히 갔어요.
examples.en: The boat went slowly along the narrow waterway.
The sound of the stream coming from the mountain is refreshing.
The course of the water changed after the typhoon.
In the old days they carried goods by water route.

explain: '강'이나 '바다'처럼 이름이 있는 큰 물이 아니라, 물이 흘러가는 길 자체를 말해요. '물길을 내다', '물길이 막히다'처럼 써요. 땅 위의 길은 '길', 바다 위 길은 '뱃길'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the path water flows along, not a named river or sea. Common uses are 물길을 내다 and 물길이 막히다. A road on land is a 길, and a route over the sea is a 뱃길.

examples.ko: 이 사진전은 한 가수의 사십 년 발자취를 보여 줘요.
examples.en: This photo exhibition shows forty years of a singer's journey.
He is following in the footsteps of his seniors.

examples.ko: 이 책은 한 시인의 발자취를 소개해요.
examples.en: This book introduces the life path of a poet.
I went to my hometown to find traces of my grandfather.
I organized our company's history in photos.

examples.ko: 역사의 발자취는 박물관에서 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can see the traces of history in the museum.

explain: 실제 걸어간 자국에도 쓰지만, 사람이나 회사가 걸어온 역사와 업적을 말할 때 더 많이 써요. '발자취를 남기다', '발자취를 따라가다'처럼 써요. 발이 땅에 남긴 모양만 말할 때는 '발자국'이 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It can mean actual footprints, but it is used more for the history and achievements of a person or company. Typical phrases are 발자취를 남기다 and 발자취를 따라가다. For only the mark a foot leaves on the ground, 발자국 is more natural.

examples.en: There was an accident, so I received insurance money.
The insurance payout will arrive within ten days.
You need documents to claim the insurance money.
I paid the hospital bill with insurance money.
I was surprised that the payout was smaller than I expected.
The insurance money was paid out to the family.

explain: 혼동하기 쉬운 말이 있어요. 매달 내는 돈은 '보험료', 사고나 병이 났을 때 받는 돈이 '보험금'이에요. '보험금을 받다/청구하다/지급하다'로 써요.
explain_en: These two are easy to mix up. The money you pay every month is 보험료, and the money you receive after an accident or illness is 보험금. The verbs are 보험금을 받다, 청구하다 and 지급하다.

examples.en: This cup is made of ceramic.
A ceramic knife is light and sharp.
A ceramic plate breaks if you drop it.
We laid ceramic tiles on the bathroom floor.

examples.ko: 세라믹 프라이팬은 음식이 잘 안 달라붙어요.
examples.en: Food doesn't stick much to a ceramic frying pan.
Ceramic products are strong against heat.

explain: 주로 제품 이름 앞에 붙어서 '세라믹 칼', '세라믹 타일'처럼 써요. 흙을 구워 만든 도자기는 '도자기'라는 말을 더 많이 쓰고, 세라믹은 기술이나 소재 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It mostly sits in front of a product name, as in 세라믹 칼 or 세라믹 타일. For traditional fired-clay ware, 도자기 is the usual word, while 세라믹 shows up in talk about technology and materials.

examples.en: I clip newspaper articles and study them.
I save articles I like right away.
I saved the article I read yesterday.
Saving good recipes is my hobby.
I'll save this post to read later.
If you don't save it, it's hard to find again.

explain: 원래는 신문 기사를 오려 붙이는 것이었는데, 요즘은 인터넷 글을 저장해 둘 때도 써요. '북마크하다', '저장하다'와 비슷하지만 스크랩은 나중에 공부하거나 참고할 자료를 모을 때 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: It originally meant cutting out newspaper articles, and now it also covers saving online posts. It is close to 북마크하다 and 저장하다, but 스크랩하다 leans toward collecting material to study or refer to later.

examples.en: My back hurt, so I went to the neurosurgery clinic.

examples.ko: 신경외과 의사가 사진을 보고 설명해 줬어요.
examples.en: The neurosurgeon looked at the scan and explained it.
This hospital's neurosurgery department is famous.
I hurt my head and was treated at neurosurgery.
Which floor is neurosurgery on?
I booked neurosurgery because of a neck disc problem.

explain: 뇌, 척추, 신경을 수술이나 시술로 치료하는 곳이에요. 허리나 목이 아플 때는 '정형외과'와 헷갈리는데, 신경 문제가 의심되면 신경외과, 뼈와 관절이면 정형외과로 가요. 약으로 신경 질환을 치료하는 곳은 '신경과'예요.
explain_en: This department treats the brain, spine and nerves with surgery or procedures. For back or neck pain people often confuse it with 정형외과: nerve problems go to 신경외과, bones and joints go to 정형외과. The one that treats nerve disease with medicine is 신경과.

examples.en: The pain of heartbreak heals only with time.

examples.ko: 그는 실연 후 한동안 말이 없었어요.
examples.en: After the breakup he was quiet for a while.
My friend got dumped, so we ate together.
I left on a trip to get over the heartbreak.

examples.ko: 이 노래는 실연한 사람의 마음을 담았어요.
examples.en: This song holds the feelings of someone who was dumped.

examples.ko: 실연 때문에 일이 손에 안 잡혀요.
examples.en: I can't focus on work because of the heartbreak.

explain: 연인과 헤어져서 아픈 마음을 말해요. 일상에서는 '이별', '헤어지다'가 더 자주 나오고, 실연은 노래나 글에서 감정을 강조할 때 많이 써요. 사랑을 얻지 못한 짝사랑의 아픔에도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is the hurt of losing a lover. In everyday talk 이별 and 헤어지다 are more common, while 실연 appears in songs and writing to stress the emotion. It can also describe the pain of unrequited love.

examples.ko: 오늘 저녁에 서울 심포니 연주회에 가요.
examples.en: I'm going to a Seoul Symphony concert this evening.

examples.ko: 그 심포니는 올해 창단 오십 주년을 맞았어요.
examples.en: That symphony orchestra marks its fiftieth anniversary this year.
A symphony orchestra is performing in Seoul.
He plays the violin in a local symphony orchestra.

examples.ko: 서울 심포니 연주를 들으면 마음이 차분해져요.
examples.en: Listening to a Seoul Symphony performance calms my mind.
This theater is famous for symphony performances.

explain: 클래식에서 '교향곡'과 같은 말이지만, 한국어에서 곡은 거의 '교향곡'이라고 하고 심포니는 '코리안심포니'처럼 악단 이름이나 영어식 느낌의 이름에 많이 나와요. 곡 이름을 말할 때는 '교향곡'이 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is the same as 교향곡 in classical music, but for the piece itself Koreans almost always say 교향곡. 심포니 shows up in orchestra names such as ○○ 심포니 오케스트라 and in Western-style titles. Use 교향곡 when you name the work.

en: win by a landslide; win overwhelmingly

examples.en: Our team won overwhelmingly in the final.
It looks like the ruling party will win big.
The opponent is weak, so we win easily by a wide margin.
He won the chess tournament by a landslide.

examples.ko: 압승하고 돌아온 선수들을 모두 박수로 맞았어요.
examples.en: Everyone welcomed the players back from their big win with applause.
If you win the first match big, you gain confidence.

explain: 점수 차나 표 차가 크게 벌어지게 이길 때 써요. 반대말은 '참패하다'예요. '대승하다'도 크게 이겼다는 뜻이지만, 선거 이야기에서는 '압승하다'가 더 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is used when you win by a big margin in score or votes. The opposite is 참패하다. 대승하다 also means a big win, but 압승하다 is more common in election news.

examples.en: This bowl is concave in the middle.
The inside of a spoon is shaped hollow.
I put the soup in a dished plate.
The ground is dented, so water collected.
The belly button is a dented part of the body.
If a mirror is concave, your face looks bigger.

explain: 가운데가 안으로 들어간 모양을 말하고, 반대로 가운데가 볼록 나온 모양은 '볼록하다'예요. 비슷한 말로 '움푹하다'는 더 깊게 푹 들어갔을 때 써요. 수학·과학에서 '오목 렌즈'로도 나와요.
explain_en: It describes a shape with the center curved inward; the opposite, bulging outward, is 볼록하다. 움푹하다 is similar but deeper. In science it appears as 오목 렌즈 (concave lens).

examples.en: Soil contains a lot of organic matter.
When fallen leaves rot, they become organic matter.
If there is a lot of organic matter in water, it smells.
Plants make organic matter by themselves.
Compost is a fertilizer made from organic matter.
In science class we learned organic and inorganic matter.

explain: 과학 시간에 '유기물'과 '무기물'을 짝으로 배워요. 생물에서 나오거나 탄소가 들어 있는 물질이 유기물이에요. 식품에서 말하는 '유기농'과 글자는 비슷해도 쓰임은 달라요.
explain_en: In science class it is learned as a pair, 유기물 and 무기물. Organic matter comes from living things or contains carbon. It looks like 유기농 (organic farming) in food talk, but they are used differently.

examples.en: On the weekend I went to the amusement park with my family.
There is a bike path in the riverside recreation area.
I bought cotton candy at the entrance of the recreation area.
That recreation park has pretty cherry blossoms in spring.
Old amusement parks had many small rides.
There are many restaurants near the recreation area, so it's convenient.

explain: 놀이기구가 있는 '놀이공원'이나 '놀이동산'보다 더 넓은 말이에요. 강가나 바닷가, 공원에 놀이기구와 식당이 있는 오래된 나들이 장소에 어울려요. 요즘은 '놀이공원'이라는 말이 더 흔해요.
explain_en: This is a broader word than 놀이공원 or 놀이동산. It suits older outing spots by rivers, seas or parks with rides and restaurants. These days 놀이공원 is the more common word.

examples.en: I learn tango every weekend.
Tango music is slow but intense.
The two people started dancing the tango.
Argentina is famous for tango.
I went to the theater to see a tango show.
In tango, two people must move as one.

explain: 춤 이름에는 '추다'를 써서 '탱고를 추다', '왈츠를 추다', '살사를 추다'처럼 말해요. '탱고를 치다'는 틀려요. 탱고는 음악 이름이기도 해서 '탱고 음악'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: Dances take the verb 추다: 탱고를 추다, 왈츠를 추다, 살사를 추다. 탱고를 치다 is wrong. 탱고 is also a music genre, so 탱고 음악 works too.

examples.en: I was physically frail as a child.
Grandma has become frail these days.
Sometimes people give herbal tonic to a frail child.
My stamina is weak, so it's hard to walk for long.

examples.ko: 그 팀은 수비가 허약해서 자주 져요.
examples.en: That team's defense is weak, so they lose often.

examples.ko: 허약하지 않으려면 운동을 꾸준히 해야 해요.
examples.en: To not be frail, you need to exercise steadily.

explain: 사람의 몸이 약해 쉽게 아플 때 써요. '약하다'보다 체질이 원래 약하다는 느낌이 강해서 건강 이야기에 어울려요. 팀의 수비처럼 힘이 부족한 조직에 비유하기도 해요.
explain_en: It describes a body that is weak and gets sick easily. It feels more constitutional than 약하다, so it fits health talk. It can also be used figuratively for an organization lacking strength, like a team's defense.

examples.en: The company announced a new guideline.
Please fill out the form according to the guideline.
The health authorities changed the mask guideline.
This guideline was made for students.
The guideline is too complicated to understand.
We work while following the guideline.

explain: 규칙처럼 꼭 지켜야 하는 것보다는 '이 방향으로 하세요' 하는 안내 기준이에요. 한국어에서는 '지침'이라는 말과 거의 같고, 가이드라인이 조금 더 가볍고 일상적이에요. '가이드라인을 따르다/지키다/만들다'로 써요.
explain_en: It is a recommended standard that says 'please go in this direction', rather than a rule you must obey. It is close to 지침, but 가이드라인 sounds a bit lighter and more everyday. Typical verbs are 따르다, 지키다 and 만들다 with it.
